traceability.notes:
The story is indeed a specification for an ESLint rule that validates @story and @req annotation format. The implementation is provided by src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts and its helper modules, with comprehensive tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts and detailed user-facing documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md.
Each listed requirement is clearly implemented and exercised: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION: Default patterns and examples for story paths and requirement IDs are defined and validated; docs and tests mirror these rules. - REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: The rule parses comment lines, identifies @story/@req/@supports, builds pending multi-line annotations, and dispatches to validators that enforce the specified syntax. - REQ-PATH-FORMAT: Story paths must match a configured regex, disallow traversal, and support suffix normalization; tests cover missing extension, wrong extension, and traversal cases. - REQ-REQ-FORMAT: Requirement IDs must match a configurable regex with default REQ-* pattern; invalid and missing IDs are reported with detailed messages, heavily tested. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: Multi-line values for both @story and @req are collapsed and validated; both valid and invalid multi-line scenarios are covered in tests. - REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: The rule works across line, block, and JSDoc comments, tolerates varying whitespace, and correctly coexists with other JSDoc tags; tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate this. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: Error builders produce clear, differentiated messages for missing vs invalid values, echo offending paths/IDs and include configured examples; tests assert the full message text.
Acceptance criteria around core functionality, quality, integration with other rules (via plugin registration and configs), user experience, error handling, and documentation are all satisfied and verified by passing automated tests. Therefore this story is fully implemented and current behavior passes all associated tests.
